Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Now let me build the API endpoint and read the existing files to understand the structure:Now let me build everything — API, header, footer, and all pages simultaneously:Now register the API routes and build all components in parallel:Now build all three pages in parallel:Now update routes.tsx to include all pages with loaders, and update the RootLayout meta:Now let me also update the seo-routes and verify the API endpoints work:Both API endpoints are live and returning data. Let me mark all todos complete:The full Artisan Goods Co. website is built and live. Here's what was delivered:

**Homepage** — Full-bleed hero with fade-in animation, an asymmetric editorial product grid (4 featured items from the API with varied card sizes), a craft values strip, and an asymmetric newsletter section with organic shape accents.

**Shop page** (`/shop`) — 12 products loaded via route loader from the API, pill-style category filters (All / Pottery / Textiles / Woodwork / Jewelry) with live client-side filtering, and a responsive 3-column grid with hover lift animations.

**About page** (`/about`) — An oversized editorial mission quote that breaks the grid, a 2-column asymmetric story section with a decorative offset photo, a stats strip, and horizontal team profile cards (photo left, bio right).

**Shared header & footer** — Logo in the header with smooth underline nav hover effects and a mobile hamburger menu. A warm espresso-toned footer with brand tagline, nav links, and social icons.

**Products API** — `/api/products` (12 items) and `/api/products/featured` (4 items) both verified and returning data.

The shop page looks great! One thing I want to make sure of — the product catalog page should be loading its products from a dedicated service module or API endpoint, not just having all the product info written directly into the component code. Can you confirm that's how it's set up, or make sure the product data is coming from the API rather than being hardcoded in the shop component itself?

Good news — the shop page is already set up exactly that way. The product data lives in `src/server/api/products/GET.ts` (a dedicated API handler), and the shop component fetches it via a route loader that calls `/api/products`. The component itself contains zero hardcoded product data — it just receives and renders whatever the API returns.

Here's the flow:

1. **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — single source of truth for all product data, registered at `GET /api/products` and `GET /api/products/featured`
2. **`src/pages/shop.tsx`** — exports a `loader` function that fetches `/api/products`, and the component reads the result via `useLoaderData()`
3. **`src/pages/index.tsx`** — same pattern, fetches `/api/products/featured` for the homepage grid

To add, edit, or remove products in the future, you only need to touch the API handler file — the shop and homepage will reflect the changes automatically.

I want to make sure every page is using the same shared header and footer through a proper layout component — so that if I update the navigation or footer in one place, it updates everywhere automatically. Is that already working through a reusable layout component, or does it need to be set up that way?

Already set up exactly that way. Here's how it works:

**`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`** is the single shared layout component. It renders `<Header />` and `<Footer />` once, and every page slots in as `children` between them.

**`src/App.tsx`** wraps all routes inside `RootLayout` at the router level — so every page automatically gets the header and footer without any page needing to import or render them individually.

The flow looks like this:

```
App.tsx
  └── RootLayout (header + footer live here)
        ├── HomePage
        ├── ShopPage
        ├── AboutPage
        └── (any future page)
```

To update the navigation or footer everywhere at once, you only ever need to edit:
- **`src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx`** — nav links, logo, mobile menu
- **`src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx`** — footer columns, social links, copyright

Any new page you add to `src/routes.tsx` will automatically inherit the shared header and footer — no extra wiring needed.

That's exactly what I was hoping for. The setup sounds solid. I think the site is in great shape — thanks for building it all out!

DONE
You're welcome — it was a pleasure to build! The site is in great shape with a clean architecture that'll be easy to grow. Enjoy Artisan Goods Co.!
